title: Address to the most pious ladies
english: An address to the most pious ladies.

I would call you an honor for the whole world, and the pride of the holy churches of Christ our common Savior — his brides, most pious and God-loved queens. The many-colored beauty of virtue flashes on you, a beauty sweet and plain to the eyes of the Godhead. Study and zeal have already brought it to pass. What remains is to shine by a right faith that nothing shakes.

Somewhere the wise Paul writes — truly learned in the law, and the one who served as priest of Christ’s mystery among the nations — “Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord.”
For where right and spotless faith keeps step with the boasts that come from good works, and the two enter on equal footing,

title: Praise deferred; virgin courts and temples
english: there you will find perfection in every good thing, and what stands sound for holiness.
So every word we have trails behind the renown that is already yours, and admits defeat without a blush. It may even deserve pardon if it fears to praise what it cannot reach.

If speech could do what it longs to do, it would stand charged with weakness for delaying. No one should clear that delay by calling it laziness. Why wound people you could have adorned with praise of virtue, by choosing silence instead?

But if speech goes slack, fears, and admits defeat, we will not blame it so much as you — you who are so public that the surpassing weight of your own brave acts has made even the speeches that usually dress everyone look like nothing.

Royal blood has come down to you from long ago, and it still runs, as we believe. Yet look: you also take hold of the kingship in Christ, and you are eager to think and to do what pleases him — shining by works and by a faith without blame, brightening your courts and the emperors’ with the glory of virginity, and raising costly temples to Christ.
He has given this too, with the rest, to your holy souls.
So I will take a word from the holy writings: “Rejoice in the Lord always; again I will say, rejoice. Let your fairness be known to all people.”
It is known, then, and cried abroad even to those throughout

title: Gift of the booklet; creed begins
english: every land and city — like an image that carries the beauty of piety toward Christ in its drawing — it has shone out clearly and been judged worthy of every wonder.

I thought I ought also to hand a spiritual gift to women already sound toward every good, as to holy brides of Christ: this little book I have freshly worked. It can give no small help, I think, to those who will read it.

Those taught — or rather talked into — wrong thoughts about Christ our common Savior it will lead back and initiate well. Those who already walk with a right mind and dwell in the doctrines of the truth it will make safer still, by many findings from good thoughts and by proofs from the God-breathed Scripture.
For the reader will learn that Emmanuel is God by nature and in truth, and that because of him the virgin who bore him is God-bearer.
Those who fear both to say this and to think it have not grasped, as one would expect, how deep the mystery of piety is.

I take it I must say in brief the apostolic and gospel tradition made concerning Christ the master of all, the aim of all God-breathed Scripture upon him, and wherever the force of the doctrines of the truth looks.

We believe, then, in one God, the Father almighty, maker of all things visible and invisible; and in one Lord, Jesus the Christ, his Son, begotten by nature from him before every age and time. title: Trinity; Word made flesh; Theotokos
english: hypostasis. We likewise believe in the Holy Spirit, not counting him a stranger to the divine nature; for he is poured out from the Father by nature through the Son upon creation.
So the holy and worshiped Trinity is understood as one, same in substance, and one in the identity of glory.

We say that this same Only-begotten Word, begotten beyond speech from the substance of God the Father, maker of the ages, the one through whom and in whom all things are, the true light, the nature that gives life to all — for he has appeared as life from the Father’s life — in the last times of the age, when the Father was pleased to save the race on earth that had fallen under a curse and been brought down by sin into death and decay, took hold of Abraham’s seed, as the Scriptures say, shared blood and flesh — that is, became human — and taking flesh and making it his own, was born in the flesh through the holy God-bearer Mary.

Yet though he became as we are and put on the slave’s form by the plan of the economy, he remained in the deity and lordship that are his by nature. He did not stop being God when he became flesh — that is, when he became as we are, a human. Because he is unchangeable by nature as God, remaining what he always was and is and will be, he has also been named Son of Man.

And since he came down willingly into the measures of humanity — for he lowered himself into emptying — he also had to endure birth from a woman. His divine nature did not take a beginning of being when he is said to have been born according to the flesh. He was, and is, as I said, the Word from God the Father by nature and in truth.

title: Theotokos; one Son; death and resurrection
english: — not a mere human begotten from her, but the Word himself enfleshed, with a body from her as his own. That is why he is said to have been begotten in the flesh: he makes the begetting of his own flesh his.

Those who senselessly deny that the holy virgin is God-bearer are forced to say there are two sons of God. For if she did not bear in the flesh the enfleshed God, they must admit — willing or not — that she bore only a common human, with nothing more than we have.

Then how will every knee bend to him, and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father? How do angels worship him, and the holy host of the highest powers? Has all heaven, with us, served a common human? God forbid.

We worship Emmanuel as true God. He is not otherwise to be worshiped unless we believe that the Word from God, whom all creation worships, became flesh according to the Scriptures — not changed into flesh, but taking flesh from the holy virgin, as I said, and enduring a human birth with us — so that, having become human, he might die for us in a human way and rise in a divine way, having trampled the power of death.

title: One death saves; one Lord, one faith, one baptism
english: holy prophets died before — famous Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Moses and Samuel, and the holy ones after them. Their death did the human race on earth no good. Christ’s death has saved it.

For he offered his own flesh for us, and by giving it to death for our sake he freed everyone from death’s bonds. One who died for all was enough — the one worth more than all — because he is by nature God, the Word from the Father, and the body offered for us as a fragrant aroma to God the Father is his own.
So it is impious, and among the wildest errors, to split the one Lord Jesus Christ into two sons. The wisest Paul will stand against them when he says: “One Lord, one faith, one baptism.”

If the Lord is one, and they then cut the one into two sons, to which do we assign the glory of lordship? To the Word sprung from the Father? The name and the reality of lordship fit him above all, and he is truly Master of all. Then where do we put the other? He will lie outside lordship, yielding to the one who already was, and who is raised beyond compare.

Or will we fasten lordship’s glory on the one from the woman, as they say when they pull them apart? Then how is the Word from God the Father Lord, if — when Scripture says there is one Lord — we hand the name of lordship to a bare human? How is there one faith? Or one baptism?
If some make two sons, in whom do we believe? Only their ignorance would invent whose name we were baptized into, when baptism is one.

title: False piety mask; many lords vs one Lord
english: and shaken into what is ugly — or rather already bent toward the last impiety.

I think that as you search his divine mystery with a sharp eye of mind, you see those who want to snatch people away. They mold a pious mask onto their own words, yet they themselves are sharper than any missile.

As far as truth’s force goes, they deny the Master who bought them — that is, Christ. But fearing the grief of those who are used to piety, and their admirable zeal, they confess that the one born from the holy virgin is also God, and Lord, and Son of God.

If a simple hearer takes their words, he will likely think they speak what is right and fitting, and not out of step with the doctrines of the truth. But if someone chooses to thin them by inquiry and put what they say to an exact test, he will not find it simple.

For “there are many gods and many lords in heaven and on earth,” as the blessed Paul writes to us, “yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things and we for him, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things and we through him.”

When we name Jesus Christ, we mean the Word from God the Father who has appeared in human form — not holding dignity as a share of grace imported from outside, but being in truth what he is believed to be.

title: Why they fear Theotokos; Athanasius cited
english: order again, and having come to be in humanity.
So if they say that the one born from the holy virgin is true God — that is, the Word from God the Father united by nature to flesh — why do they fear to confess that the holy virgin is God-bearer?

Their aim is to pretend and say, “Yes, he is also God and Lord and sits with the Father,” while they do not think so in truth. They say the glory of sonship and lordship was given, as a share of grace and by advancement, to a common human like us born from the holy virgin.

But the word God-bearer was already customary even with the holy fathers before us, who are admired for right faith, and still with all under heaven, so to speak. I thought I had to declare that as true.

So that I may not seem to say whatever comes to mind without testing it, I have gathered from the books they wrote in the churches what serves this point, set it beside my case as proof, and will seal my own words into the truth.

title: Athanasius: one Son; flesh suffers, deity impassible
english: — worshiped, and worshiped with his flesh in one worship. Not two sons: one a true Son of God who is worshiped, and another a human from Mary who is not worshiped, made a son of God by grace as humans are. But the one from God, as I said — one Son of God and God, himself and no other — also born from Mary according to the flesh in the last days, as the angel said to the God-bearer Mary when she asked, “How will this be, since I do not know a man?” — “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the holy one who is born will be called Son of God.”

So the one born from the holy virgin is Son of God by nature and true God, not by grace and sharing. Only according to the flesh from Mary is he human; according to the Spirit he himself is Son of God and God.

He suffered our sufferings according to the flesh, as it is written, “Christ suffered for us in the flesh,” and again, “He who did not spare his own Son, but handed him over for us all.” Yet he remained impassible and unchanged according to the deity, as the prophet says: “I am God, and I do not change.”

title: Athanasius anathemas; Atticus on kenosis
english: remaining beyond death’s grasp because of the deity.

“But if anyone teaches otherwise from the divine Scriptures — saying one son of God and another, the human from Mary made a son by grace as we are, so that there are two sons, one Son of God by nature from God, and one by grace, the human from Mary — or if anyone says our Lord’s flesh is from above and not from the virgin Mary, or that the deity was turned into flesh, or confused, or altered, or passible, or that our Lord’s flesh is not to be worshiped as a human’s flesh, and not worshipable as the flesh of Lord and God — the holy catholic church anathematizes that person, persuaded by the divine apostle who says, ‘If anyone proclaims to you a gospel contrary to what you received, let him be anathema.’”
So much for the blessed Athanasius. I think I should also set beside him voices of other holy bishops with the same aim.

From bishop Atticus: “Today Christ the Master took on the birth that belongs to love of humankind; the worth of deity was already his.” Then he adds again: “The Word of love for humankind is emptied, though his nature cannot be emptied; for he emptied himself, taking a slave’s form. The fleshless one is enfleshed for you; for the Word became flesh. He who cannot be touched, because his nature is bodiless, is handled. The one without beginning comes under a bodily beginning. The perfect one grows. The unchangeable advances. The rich one is born in an inn. He who wraps the heaven in clouds is wrapped in swaddling cloths.”

title: Antiochus; Amphilochius; Ammonius
english: From bishop Antiochus: “For yesterday, in undefiled birth pangs, the life-bearer, the fair-bearer, the great-bearer, the light-bearer, the hope-bearer, the God-bearer, the strange-bearer, the virgin-mother Mary brought us a Savior.”

From Amphilochius, bishop of Iconium, from the treatise on the birth according to the flesh: “The truth was made known, grace came, and life appeared. The Son of God, the Word from God, became flesh for us, so that he might raise mortals into eternal life and wake them from the dead. The maker of all things, who is before all creation, visible and invisible, coexisting immortal with the Father alone and the Spirit — see, today he is born to us from a virgin, without any sin, without a human father.”

From Ammonius, bishop of Adrianople: “For he too said somewhere about the Word of God: But if he himself is God by nature, as God’s Only-begotten Son, and in taking the slave’s form was also counted worthy to be called firstborn son of the holy virgin, he gave himself as a ransom for all.” He goes on: “I have already shown the impiety into which the Arians fall when they say the God-bearer Mary needed the sacrifices then offered under the law for women who give birth.”

title: Chrysostom; Severianus; Vitalis
english: From John, bishop of Constantinople, on the divine birth. He says of the holy virgin: “Instead of a sun, he says, she contains without limit the sun of righteousness. Nature’s order is overcome; for he willed, he was able, he came down, he saved — all things run together for God. Today the One who is is born, and the One who is becomes what he was not. Being God, he becomes human without leaving off being God. He did not become human by departing from deity, nor become God by climbing up from humanity. Being Word, he became flesh without suffering change; his nature remained unchanged.” He adds: “He who sits on a high and lifted throne is laid in a manger. The untouchable, simple, bodiless one is wrapped by human hands. He who breaks the bonds of sin is tangled in swaddling cloths.”

From bishop Severianus: “For the Word begotten from above from the Father — beyond speech, beyond telling, beyond grasp, eternally — is himself begotten in time from below from the virgin Mary, so that those first born from below may be born from above from a second birth, that is, from God.”
